svg.aria-label: Diagram: An AWS resource group stores a query rather than a list of members. AWS describes it as the query used to dynamically define the members of a group, and defines a group as a collection of AWS resources that are all in the same AWS Region and that match the criteria specified in the group's query. There are two query types. TAG_FILTERS_1_0 is tag-based, where any resources with tags that match are automatically part of the group, and its membership changes through a console tag edit. CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_1_0 is the default and bases membership on a single CloudFormation stack, since you can base your query on only one stack, so its membership changes through a deployment that leaves a record. Membership can change three ways with no edit to the group at all: someone adds a matching tag and the resource joins, someone removes one and the resource leaves while the run still reports complete, or AWS adds support for a new resource type and an all-supported-types group grows on AWS's release schedule. AWS warns that in that last case the actions might run on many more resources than were in the group when you first created the group. Whatever reads the group acts on the current answer, including Systems Manager bulk actions on applications based on resource groups, VPC Network Access Analyzer which uses a group as a scope's sources and destinations, and EC2 Capacity Reservations where a later matching reservation automatically moves a running instance into reserved capacity. Tag-based queries combine tags with AND, so every filter added narrows the group rather than widening it. Quotas are 100 resource groups per account in each supported Region and adjustable, 15 GetResources calls per second, 5 calls per second on the tagging write operations which are not adjustable in the console, and 50 user created tags per resource. The closing rule is that groups you read can be broad and dynamic while groups you execute should be explicit and reviewed.
svg.title: A group is a question, not a set
svg.text: A group stores a query. The answer is computed when something reads it.
“The query used to dynamically define the members of a group.”
TAG_FILTERS_1_0
“any resources with tags that match are
automatically part of the group”
Membership moves on a console tag edit
— recorded as a tag change, not a membership one.
CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_1_0 — “the default”
“You can base your query on only one
CloudFormation stack”
Membership moves on a deployment
— a reviewed change-management boundary.
Three ways the membership changes with no edit to the group
someone adds a tag the resource joins, and whatever acts on the group reaches it
someone removes a tag the resource leaves, and the next run still reports complete
AWS adds a type an all-supported-types group grows on AWS’s release schedule
“the actions might run on many more resources than were in the group when you first
created the group” — AWS, on the page where you make that choice
Whatever reads the group acts on the current answer
Systems Manager “take bulk actions on your applications that are based on
resource groups” — a host that left is a host not patched
Network Analyzer the group is the scope’s sources and destinations
Capacity Reservation a later matching reservation moves a running instance into it
AND, not OR
Tags are combined with AND, so every filter you
add narrows the group. Being more precise
makes it less complete.
Quotas, and one of them paces remediation
100 groups per account per Region, adjustable.
15 GetResources per second; 5 per second on the
tagging writes, and that one is not adjustable.
Groups you read can be broad and dynamic. Groups you execute should be explicit and reviewed.
The two look identical in the console, so the division has to be yours. A group sounds like a set; it is a question.
